answer: We formalize a Sybil-resistant protocol where each identity threads a dynamic opportunity-cost bond B(t) scaling with cumulative adversarial density, making mass identity creation prohibitively expensive; deviation triggers subgame-perfect slashing of the full bond plus a penalty λ, so expected payoff is strictly negative. Under capital barrier analysis, the marginal cost of partitioning any canyon of trust exceeds the supralinear bond, and no finite discount can justify a haven of profitable deviation, so identity multiplication is dominated.
